name: Accuracy cost of quantization: measured deltas on named benchmarks
activation_scheme: This record summarizes the measured accuracy deltas from the literature. Most quantization papers report speed but omit accuracy. The following are the sources that DO report measured accuracy delta on a named benchmark.
quality_delta: SUMMARY OF MEASURED ACCURACY DELTAS: (1) Marlin INT4 (Llama2-7B, WikiText-2): 5.12 (FP16) vs 5.27 (INT4) = +0.15 ppl. MMLU: 41.80 vs 40.07 = -1.73. (2) GPTQ 3-bit (Llama-7B, WikiText-2): 5.68 (FP16) vs 8.07 (3-bit) = +2.39 ppl. With group-128: 6.61 = +0.93 ppl. (3) SpQR 3-4 bit (LLaMA, Falcon): <1% perplexity loss. (4) SignRound 2-bit: 6.91-33.22% improvement over RTN across 11 tasks. (5) LLM-FP4 (LLaMA-13B, commonsense zero-shot): 63.1 vs 68.9 (FP16) = -5.8 points. (6) SpinQuant W4A4KV4 (LLaMA-2-7B, zero-shot): 64.0 vs 66.9 (FP16) = -2.9 points. (7) QuaRot W4A4KV4 (LLaMA2-70B, WikiText-2): 0.29-0.47 ppl increase. (8) KIVI 2-bit KV: 'almost the same quality' (qualitative). (9) KVQuant 3-bit KV: <0.1 ppl degradation. (10) AWQ INT3 (OPT-6.7B, WikiText-2): 43.2 (RTN) vs 13.0 (AWQ) = -30.2 ppl improvement over RTN. The pattern: 4-bit weight-only quantization typically costs 0.1-0.3 ppl on WikiText-2. 3-bit costs 0.5-1.0 ppl. 2-bit costs 2.0+ ppl. KV cache quantization at 4-bit is nearly lossless; at 2-3-bit it costs 0.1-0.5 ppl. The accuracy cost is model-dependent and benchmark-dependent.
notes:
PROXY ENUM VALUE - DECLARED 2026-10-04 (minor): this is a cross-method SUMMARY of measured accuracy deltas, filed under 'gptq'. Its three sources are Marlin, SpQR and SignRound, of which only SpQR and SignRound are GPTQ-adjacent and neither IS GPTQ. Use it for the accuracy comparison, not as a GPTQ record. GROUP SIZE LEFT NULL 2026-10-04: this is a SUMMARY record that aggregates measured accuracy deltas across methods whose group sizes differ (the underlying records are gptq-128, spqr-128, signround-128). Recording one value would attribute a single configuration to a cross-method comparison. This record addresses the repo's priority: 'most of this literature reports speed and omits accuracy - prioritize sources that report measured accuracy DELTA on a named benchmark.' The summary above is compiled from the records in this repo. The key finding: 4-bit weight-only quantization is nearly lossless for most models (0.1-0.3 ppl), but 3-bit and below show significant degradation. KV cache quantization at 4-bit is nearly lossless, but at 2-3-bit the accuracy cost is model-dependent. The most dramatic accuracy delta is SignRound's 6.91-33.22% improvement at 2-bit, which shows that optimized rounding matters enormously at very low bit widths. The least documented area is FP8/FP4 KV cache quantization, where no controlled benchmark with named accuracy delta was found. This is a significant gap in the literature.

Rule of thumb for this field everywhere in the repo: if the bits field carries an 'a16', or the scheme is KV-cache-only or a llama.cpp integer storage type, an empty native_support is a DEFINITION and needs no verification; only a W4A4/W8A8/sub-8-bit format with research kernels can have an empty list that is a real finding.
